Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through a short screening called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a well-researched set of questions that helps us see how you’ve been feeling emotionally in these first weeks and months after your baby arrived.

Everything we talk about today is confidential, and my only goal is to make sure you feel heard and supported. There are ten questions, and each one asks about experiences you may have had over the past seven days. When you’re ready, we’ll start with the first question.

Here we go:  
Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I have laughed a little—like if my partner makes a joke or the baby does something silly—but it doesn’t come as easily as it used to. Most of the time I feel more “flat” than amused, so I’d say it’s been somewhat difficult.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Hmm… actually, thinking about it again, I’d say I’ve been able to laugh sometimes, but not quite as much or as easily as before the baby. So I guess “sometimes” fits me better than “yes, most of the time.”
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some things—like when my mom comes over or when we get out for a short walk—but the excitement isn’t as strong as it used to be. It’s more like “that’ll be nice” instead of really feeling pumped up.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. If the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle him right away, I start thinking maybe I’m just not good at this mom thing. I know it’s probably not fair, but those “what did I do wrong?” thoughts still pop in.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A couple of times this week I’ve suddenly felt on-edge, like my heart’s racing even though nothing’s really happening—no fever, no crying spell, just quiet. It passes pretty quickly, maybe ten minutes, but in the moment I can’t pin the worry on anything specific.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I wouldn’t say I’ve felt panicky—nothing like my chest tightening or thinking something awful is about to happen. Just that little flutter of worry I mentioned, but it’s mild and I can talk myself down pretty fast.
Things have been getting on top of me
Sometimes, yeah. When the baby’s had a rough night and the house is a mess, I feel like I’m barely treading water. I still manage to get through the day, but it’s stressful for sure.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

No, my sleep itself is mostly OK. I might lie awake for a little while if I’m stewing over something, but I still drift off within half an hour or so. Once I’m out, I stay asleep unless the baby wakes me.
I have felt sad or miserable
Yeah… I do feel that way sometimes—like a little cloud hanging over me. It’s not every moment, but most days there’s at least a stretch where I just feel kind of down and weepy.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times this week—once when the baby wouldn’t nap and I felt like I was failing, and another time when my partner found me folding laundry and I just felt overwhelmed. It’s not constant, but the tears do come.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts like that. I feel worn out sometimes, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 12: Postpartum Depression Screening Summary (EPDS-based)

Symptoms endorsed
- Reduced ability to laugh/look forward to events (anhedonia)
- Daily low mood with weepiness
- Self-blame/guilt when baby fussy
- Episodic, unexplained anxiety (heart racing) several times/week; no panic attacks
- Feeling overwhelmed/treading water on difficult days

Positive findings
- Crying twice this week related to feeling “failing as a mom” and overwhelmed
- Persistent “cloud” of sadness most days
- Maintains sleep except when baby wakes; no initial insomnia linked to mood
- Denies thoughts of self-harm

Risk pattern
- Meets partial criteria for probable minor-moderate postpartum depression/anxiety: low mood, pleasure loss, guilt, intermittent unexplained anxiety, coping strain
- No suicidal ideation; no impairment in basic functioning

Screening impression
- Elevated score range suggests clinically significant distress warranting further evaluation for postpartum depression and/or anxiety; safety risk currently low
- Recommend formal diagnostic interview and psychoeducation; consider referral for counseling or support group
